en: In the summer of 1942 two forces invaded Egypt, and each provoked a decisive battle. Only one of the two was human, so only that one is remembered, although the casualties in the other battle were greater. On the northwest coast, Erwin Rommel’s Afrika Corps crossed the border from Libya and was halted on its march toward Cairo by the British Eighth Army at al-Alamein. Four months later the British counterattacked. After a two-week tank battle they routed the German and Italian forces, whom they outnumbered in men and tanks by more than two to one. Al-Alamein was the Allies’ first decisive land victory in World War II and, along with the Soviet victory a month later at Stalingrad, appeared to turn the tide of the war. No count of the casualties was possible given the scale of violence and the disarray among the defeated forces, but somewhere between fifty and seventy thousand soldiers may have been killed, wounded, or missing.

Long after the armies moved on, moreover, the battle continued to claim its victims. Al-Alamein marked the first use of land mines as a major weapon of war. It was responsible for three-quarters of the twenty-three million uncleared mines Egypt accumulated in the twentieth century, the largest number of any country in the world.
zh: 1942年夏天，两股力量入侵了埃及，各自引发了一场决定性的战斗。其中只有一股力量由人组成，所以只有那一场战斗被人铭记，尽管另一场战斗造成的伤亡更大。在西北海岸，埃尔温·隆美尔的非洲军团从利比亚越过边境，向开罗进军，却在阿拉曼被英国第八集团军挡住。四个月后，英军发动反攻。经过两周的坦克战，英军击溃了德军和意军；其兵力和坦克数量均超过对方两倍。阿拉曼是盟军在第二次世界大战中取得的第一场决定性的陆战胜利，与一个月后苏军在斯大林格勒的胜利一道，似乎扭转了战争局势。由于暴力的规模之大，以及战败部队的混乱，伤亡人数无法统计，但阵亡、受伤或失踪的士兵可能有五万至七万人。
而且，在军队开走很久之后，这场战斗仍在夺取生命。阿拉曼标志着地雷首次被用作战争的主要武器。埃及在20世纪积存了2300万枚尚未清除的地雷，数量居世界之首，其中四分之三源于这场战役。

en: Meanwhile, at the other end of the country another invader arrived, descending down the Nile valley from Sudan: the
a mosquito native to sub-Saharan Africa but previously unknown in Egypt. The gambiae mosquito carried in its stomach the malignant form of the malaria parasite,

Other species of malarial mosquitoes existed in Egypt, but these carried a more benign form of malaria and were confined to small pockets in the north, where the local population had developed a degree of immunity. There were no local defenses against

The first reports of an outbreak of gambiae malaria came in March 1942 from the villages of Nubia, the country lying across Egypt’s southern border with Sudan. The epidemic reached Aswan by July and Luxor by August, then continued north to Asyut, the largest city in the south. As at al-Alamein, the number of victims was unknown and unknowable. It was estimated that three-quarters of a million people may have contracted the disease in the three years of the epidemic, and between one and two hundred thousand died.
zh: 与此同时，在这个国家的另一端，又有一个入侵者从苏丹沿尼罗河谷顺流而下：冈比亚按蚊（Anopheles gambiae）。这种蚊子原产于撒哈拉以南非洲，此前在埃及却不为人知。冈比亚按蚊胃内携带着一种恶性的疟疾寄生虫——恶性疟原虫（Plasmodium falciparum）。

埃及原本也有其他种类的传疟蚊，但它们传播的是较为温和的疟疾，而且局限于北方的一些小片地区，当地人口已经形成了一定程度的免疫力。对于恶性疟原虫，当地却没有防御能力。1942年3月，横跨埃及与苏丹南部边界的努比亚地区，其村庄首次传出了冈比亚按蚊所致疟疾暴发的报告。疫情7月抵达阿斯旺，8月抵达卢克索，随后继续向北，到达南方最大的城市艾斯尤特。与阿拉曼一样，受害人数既不为人知，也无从确知。据估计，在疫情持续的三年中，可能有75万人感染，十万至二十万人死亡。

en: I first heard about the 1942 malaria invasion in 1989 from a man named ʿAmm Ibrahim, who lived in a village near Luxor where I was spending time.

Then in his eighties, he was the most informed narrator of the history of the village, and the story of the malaria epidemic was always the most vivid part of his narrative. It killed one-third of the village, he used to say, and there were not enough healthy men left alive even to carry the dead. People were hauled to their graves on the back of a camel.
zh: 我第一次听说1942年的疟疾入侵，是1989年听一位名叫阿姆·易卜拉欣的人讲起的。他住在卢克索附近的一个村庄，我当时正在那里生活。
他那时已经八十多岁，是最熟悉村庄历史的讲述者，而疟疾流行的故事总是他叙述中最鲜明的部分。他常说，疟疾夺走了村里三分之一人的生命，活着的健康男子甚至不够抬走死者。人们用骆驼驮着死者，把他们运到墓地。

en: The war and the epidemic interacted with a third threat to the country, a severe wartime shortage of food. The shortage had complex causes of its own. In 1933 the dam across the river Nile at Aswan, built at the turn of the century, had been increased in height, completing a network of dams, barrages, and canals begun in the mid-nineteenth century that converted most of the country’s agricultural land to year-round irrigation.

Only one-fifth of the Nile valley was now irrigated by the river’s annual flood, which in the past had fertilized the soil by depositing a layer of silt and nutrients. The other four-fifths required chemical fertilizers.
By the end of the 1930s Egyptian farmers were using 600,000 tons of fertilizer a year— mostly the new artificial nitrates—at the highest rate per cultivated area in the world.

An international cartel among chemical manufacturers had assigned 80 percent of the Egyptian market to a consortium led by the German business group I. G. Farben, one of whose companies had invented the process for synthesizing ammonium nitrate.
These supplies were cut off by the outbreak of war.
zh: 战争与疫情还同威胁这个国家的第三种力量相互作用，即战时严重的粮食短缺。这种短缺本身有着复杂的成因。1933年，世纪之交建在阿斯旺、横跨尼罗河的大坝被加高，至此，一个始于19世纪中叶、由大坝、拦河闸与运河组成的网络建成，使全国大部分农田改用全年灌溉。
如今，尼罗河谷只有五分之一的土地仍由河流一年一度的洪水灌溉；过去，洪水沉积一层淤泥与养分，使土壤保持肥力。其余五分之四的土地则需要化学肥料。
到20世纪30年代末，埃及农民每年使用60万吨肥料——主要是新型人工合成硝酸盐——单位耕地面积的使用量居世界之首。
化学品制造商组成的国际卡特尔，将埃及市场的80%划给了一个由德国法本工业集团（I. G. Farben）领衔的联合体；该集团的一家公司发明了合成硝酸铵的工艺。
战争爆发切断了这些供应。
body.review: 本章引用的统计和医学判断均属于2002年底本的历史叙述。化学名称中的明显疑点保留原文，并在下文相应位置说明。

en: The lack of fertilizer caused the yield of wheat and other crops to drop by as much as a quarter. The government introduced food rationing to supply the cities and the British troops, and introduced fertilizer rationing and acreage controls to force landowners to switch half the country’s cotton fields to the cultivation of food.

In the far south, however, the main commercial crop was sugarcane rather than cotton, for which no controls were introduced. The owners of the cane plantations extended the crop’s acreage by as much as 30 percent during the war, exacerbating the shortage of staple foods in the region hit by gambiae malaria (and increasing the breeding grounds for mosquitoes).

In the second year of the malaria epidemic casualties were much higher, since many households had been too sick to harvest the previous year’s food crop and were weakened by famine and malnutrition. The highest casualty rates were recorded among the workers on the sugar estates.

At one of the largest cane plantations, a few miles south of Luxor, the manager estimated that malaria affected 80 to 90 percent of the people, and the doctor in the nearby town of Armant reported eighty to ninety deaths a day.
zh: 肥料匮乏使小麦及其他作物的产量下降了多达四分之一。政府实行粮食配给，以供应城市和英国军队，又实行肥料配给与种植面积管制，迫使土地所有者把全国一半的棉田改种粮食。
然而，在最南部，主要的商品作物是甘蔗而非棉花，甘蔗并未受到管制。战争期间，甘蔗种植园主把种植面积扩大了多达30%，加剧了冈比亚按蚊疟疾肆虐地区主食的短缺，也增加了蚊虫的孳生地。
疫情第二年的伤亡要高得多，因为许多家庭上一年病得无法收获粮食，此后又因饥荒和营养不良而衰弱。糖业庄园工人的伤亡率最高。
在卢克索以南几英里处一个规模最大的甘蔗种植园中，经理估计有80%至90%的人感染了疟疾；附近阿尔曼特镇的医生则报告，每天有八十至九十人死亡。

en: The elements combining to cause the disaster of 1942–44 represented some of the most powerful transformations of the twentieth century. First, there was the damming of the river. The building of the original barrage at Aswan in 1898–1902 helped inaugurate around the world an era of engineering on a new scale. Schemes to block the flow of large rivers were to become the century’s largest construction projects. Dams were unique in the scope and manner in which they altered the distribution of resources across space and time, among entire communities and ecosystems. They offered more than just a promise of agricultural development or technical progress. For many postcolonial governments, this ability to rearrange the natural and social environment became a means to demonstrate the strength of the modern state as a techno-economic power.

Second, there were the synthetic chemicals. The manufacture of artificial nitrates introduced a transformation even greater than the building of dams. From the largely synthetic-free world of 1925, the production of new chemicals, led by nitrates, grew at a phenomenal rate. In the United States output increased tenfold in each decade. By the 1980s there were four million synthetic chemicals in production, sixty thousand of which were in common use. This transformation had an impact at the level of the cell and the organism to rival that of dams at the national level.
Third, there was malaria, which took advantage of irrigation schemes, population movements, and changes in agriculture to become the world’s most deadly infectious disease.

represented only 30 percent of clinical malaria cases but was responsible for up to 90 percent of the deaths. It was so widespread that no one could agree even to the nearest million how many lives it was taking each year.

Finally, there was the war. Al-Alamein was remembered as the first great mechanized conflict, in which the German panzers, used in new kinds of tactical combination with antitank guns and aircraft, engaged the larger Grant and Sherman tanks. Yet the battle front was so narrow, and the German and Italian machinery so short of fuel and ammunition, that the two-week battle was fought at close quarters, like a battle of World War I. It epitomized a new and lethal interaction of man and machine.
zh: 共同造成1942—1944年灾难的各种因素，代表着20世纪一些最强有力的转变。首先是河流筑坝。1898—1902年阿斯旺最初那座拦河坝的兴建，帮助开启了全球工程规模空前扩大的时代。截断大河水流的计划，将成为这个世纪规模最大的建设项目。大坝改变资源在空间与时间上、在整个社区与生态系统之间的分配，其范围和方式独一无二。它们许下的不仅是农业发展或技术进步的承诺。对于许多后殖民政府而言，这种重新安排自然与社会环境的能力，成为展示现代国家作为技术—经济力量之实力的手段。
其次是合成化学品。人工硝酸盐的制造带来的转变，比筑坝还要巨大。从1925年那个基本没有合成物的世界出发，以硝酸盐为首的新化学品产量以惊人的速度增长。在美国，产量每十年就增长十倍。到20世纪80年代，投入生产的合成化学品达四百万种，其中六万种被普遍使用。这种转变在细胞和有机体层面的影响，足以与大坝在国家层面的影响相匹敌。
第三是疟疾。它借助灌溉计划、人口流动和农业变化，成为世界上最致命的传染病。恶性疟原虫引起的病例仅占临床疟疾病例的30%，却造成了高达90%的死亡。其传播如此广泛，以至于它每年夺走多少生命，连精确到百万位都无法达成共识。
最后是战争。阿拉曼被铭记为第一场大规模机械化冲突：德国坦克以新型战术与反坦克炮、飞机协同，迎战体型更大的格兰特和谢尔曼坦克。然而，战线过于狭窄，德意两军的机械装备又缺乏燃料和弹药，因此这场为期两周的战斗以近距离交战展开，仿佛第一次世界大战中的一场战斗。它集中体现了人与机器之间一种新出现的致命互动。

en: Dams, blood-borne parasites, synthetic chemicals, mechanized war, and man-made famine coincided and interacted. It is not surprising to find disease brought by environmental transformation, industrial chemistry shaped by military needs, or war accompanied by famine. Nevertheless, their interaction presents a challenge. How exactly did tanks and parasites and synthetic nitrates affect one another? What kind of explanation can bring them together?
zh: 大坝、血液传播的寄生虫、合成化学品、机械化战争与人为饥荒，同时出现并相互作用。环境转变带来疾病、工业化学受军事需要塑造，或战争伴随饥荒，这些现象并不令人惊讶。然而，它们的相互作用提出了一个难题：坦克、寄生虫与合成硝酸盐究竟如何彼此影响？怎样的解释才能把它们联系起来？

en: The war and the epidemic interacted on several levels. At the outbreak of hostilities Britain had reimposed martial law on Egypt, after the country had enjoyed almost two decades of partial independence from the colonial occupation established in 1882. The authorities censored reporting of the malaria epidemic, hoping to contain it in the south. Already preparing to evacuate Cairo in case Rommel broke through at al-Alamein, the British were unwilling to divert men and resources from the north to meet the invader from the south. This helped the gambiae mosquito advance. The British also faced a shortage of quinine, the only treatment against the infection, for in the same month that gambiae malaria was reported in Nubia the Japanese had occupied Java, cutting off the Dutch cinchona plantations whose trees supplied the drug to Europe.

So the Egyptian Ministry of Health was left to launch its own antimalaria campaign. Its eradication teams attacked the disease vector—the mosquito—rather than the parasite itself, spreading Malariol, diesel oil mixed with a spreading agent, on pools of standing water. The oil formed a film on the water surface, which prevented the mosquito larvae from hatching. Malariol tended to go missing, however, since irrigation pumps could use the diesel oil as fuel, which the war had made it difficult to obtain. The eradication teams later replaced it with Paris green, a mixture of arsenic powder and copper acetate used originally as a painters’ pigment, which proved a more reliable larvicide, or at least one less liable to be taken over for other purposes.
zh: 战争与疫情在若干层面相互作用。战事爆发时，英国重新在埃及实施戒严，此前埃及在摆脱始于1882年的殖民占领后，已经享有将近二十年的部分独立。当局审查有关疟疾疫情的报道，希望把疫情限制在南方。英国人已在准备一旦隆美尔突破阿拉曼便撤出开罗，不愿从北方调拨人员和资源去对付来自南方的入侵者。这帮助了冈比亚按蚊的推进。英方还面临奎宁短缺，这是当时唯一的抗疟治疗药物；就在努比亚报告冈比亚按蚊疟疾的同一个月，日本占领了爪哇，切断了荷兰金鸡纳树种植园的供货，而欧洲的奎宁正是从这些树木中取得的。

于是，埃及卫生部只能自行发动抗疟运动。灭蚊队针对的是疾病媒介——蚊子——而非寄生虫本身：他们在积水池中撒布Malariol，即掺有铺展剂的柴油。油在水面形成一层薄膜，阻止蚊幼虫孵化。不过，Malariol经常不翼而飞，因为灌溉水泵可用其中的柴油作为燃料，而战争使燃料难以获得。灭蚊队后来改用巴黎绿，即砷粉与醋酸铜的混合物，原先用作绘画颜料。事实证明，它是一种更可靠的杀幼虫剂，或者至少更不容易被挪作他用。
body.review: 底本写的是阻止幼虫‘孵化’（larvae from hatching）。按蚊生命周期为卵、幼虫、蛹、成虫，严格说孵化的是卵；此处保留作者措辞。

en: The war may even have brought the epidemic. The anopheles mosquito has a range of only two miles, so to reach Egypt it needed vectors of its own. One view was that it must have arrived by airplane, a mode of travel not unusual for mosquitoes. German air and submarine attacks had made the Mediterranean unsafe, so the British were flying a new supply route to Cairo via West Africa and Sudan. But the hostilities may also have enabled the mosquito to reach Egypt by boat. The war had increased river traffic with Sudan, and the building and raising of the Aswan Dam had created new breeding places for the insect along the route. Once in Egypt, the mosquito continued to travel north, moving by boat, train, and motorcar. To prevent its movement, these vehicles were treated by a new technique, the pyrethrum spray, developed over the previous decade to combat a major outbreak of malaria in Natal Province on the east coast of South Africa— like Upper Egypt, a region producing sugarcane. Pyrethrum powder, made of the dried flowers of the pyrethrum variety of chrysanthemum and sometimes burned to fumigate houses against insects, was mixed with green soap and glycerine and then forced through the spray nozzle of a stirrup pump, making a fine poisonous mist that killed the adult mosquitoes.
zh: 甚至可能是战争本身带来了疫情。按蚊的活动范围只有两英里，因此，要抵达埃及，它自己也需要传播媒介。一种看法认为，它必定是乘飞机而来；蚊子搭乘飞机并非罕见。德军的空袭与潜艇袭击使地中海不再安全，因此英国人开辟了一条经西非和苏丹飞往开罗的补给航线。但战事也可能使蚊子得以乘船抵达埃及。战争增加了与苏丹之间的河运，阿斯旺大坝的修建与加高又沿途为昆虫创造了新的孳生地。一旦进入埃及，蚊子便乘船、火车和汽车继续北上。为阻止其移动，人们用一种新技术——除虫菊喷雾——处理这些交通工具。这项技术是在此前十年中，为应对南非东海岸纳塔尔省一次严重的疟疾暴发而开发的；该省同上埃及一样，是一个甘蔗产区。除虫菊粉由除虫菊的干花制成，有时也被焚烧以熏杀屋内害虫；人们将其与绿皂及甘油混合，再用脚踏固定的手压泵从喷嘴喷出，形成细密的毒雾，杀死成蚊。

en: Disease often moves with the changing movements of people, and modern war causes large numbers to find routes outside existing networks of trade and migration. But having taken advantage of new kinds of transport and traffic routes, the insect also needed ways to establish itself by colonizing new territory and populations. The patterns of war and transportation had to intersect with other developments, in particular changing hydraulics. In the same years that the gambiae mosquito began to move north from equatorial Africa along the Upper Nile valley, it also crossed the Atlantic to the coast of Brazil. In both Brazil and the Upper Nile the mosquito took advantage of recent irrigation works and changed patterns of water use. In the case of the Nile, the British had extended the control of the river at Aswan by constructing further storage reservoirs in the Anglo-Egyptian-occupied Sudan. Dams were completed across the Blue Nile at Sennar, two hundred miles south of Khartoum, the Sudanese capital, in 1925, and across the White Nile at Jabal Aulia, thirty miles above Khartoum, in 1937. These projects were followed by reports of new levels of endemic disease, including schistosomiasis (a parasitic worm infection carried by an aquatic snail that would eventually affect all of Egypt, and whose treatment later introduced another endemic infection, hepatitis C, in possibly the world’s largest transmission of blood-borne pathogens from medical intervention) as well as malaria.

The linking together of the river control projects enabled the mosquito to jump barriers from one region to the next. The accompanying cultivation based on perennial irrigation created many breeding places among a thicker population of human hosts that often lived much closer to the water now that flooding no longer occurred in many areas. The engineers who built the irrigation works had not considered the possibility that snails or mosquitoes would make use of their work to move, or that certain parasites would travel with these hosts, or that devastating consequences would ensue. In a private report in 1942, however, the British acknowledged that the surest way to restore the health of the Egyptian population would be to destroy the dams and return to basin irrigation.
zh: 疾病往往随人群流动方式的改变而移动，现代战争又迫使大批人口在既有贸易与迁移网络之外另寻路径。然而，这种昆虫在利用新型交通工具与运输路线之后，还需要通过进入新的地域和人群来立足。战争与交通的模式必须同其他变化交织在一起，尤其是水流系统的变化。就在冈比亚按蚊开始从赤道非洲沿上尼罗河谷北移的那些年里，它也跨越了大西洋，到达巴西海岸。在巴西和上尼罗河地区，蚊子都利用了新近的灌溉工程和用水模式的改变。在尼罗河，英国人通过在英埃占领下的苏丹增建蓄水库，扩大了阿斯旺水利工程对河流的控制。1925年，位于苏丹首都喀土穆以南二百英里的森纳尔，建成了横跨青尼罗河的大坝；1937年，在喀土穆上游三十英里的杰贝勒奥利亚，又建成了横跨白尼罗河的大坝。工程完成后，地方病发病水平上升的报告随之出现，包括疟疾和血吸虫病。后者是一种由水生螺传播的寄生虫感染，最终波及整个埃及；其治疗后来又引入了另一种地方性感染——丙型肝炎，这可能是世界上由医疗干预造成的最大规模血液传播病原体传播事件。

河流控制工程相互连通，使蚊子能够跨越障碍，从一个地区抵达另一个地区。随之发展的常年灌溉农业创造了大量孳生地，其间生活着更为稠密的人类宿主；由于许多地区不再泛滥，人们往往住得离水边更近。修建灌溉工程的工程师没有考虑到，螺或蚊子可能利用他们的工程迁移，某些寄生虫可能随这些宿主移动，或者由此产生毁灭性的后果。然而，英国人在1942年的一份内部报告中承认，要恢复埃及人口的健康，最可靠的办法就是拆除大坝，回到盆地灌溉。

en: The irrigation works led to other unexpected effects. The damming of the river altered the distribution and timing of its flow, as well as the temperature and chemistry of the water. This affected the riverbed and banks, altering the character of the riverine environment. Microorganisms and plants dependent on the balance of the river’s ebb and flood disappeared, while other, more aggressive species took advantage of the change. Curly pondweed, or
one of the most invasive aquatic plants, began to form large islands of weed, which the river’s current carried in clumps downstream. An Egyptian malaria expert established that the
in turn made use of the pondweed, which transported the larvae of the mosquito from one breeding area to the next.
zh: 灌溉工程还产生了其他意料之外的影响。筑坝改变了河流流量的分布和时间节律，也改变了水温与水的化学性质。这些变化影响河床与河岸，改变了河流环境的特征。依赖河流涨落平衡的微生物和植物消失了，另一些更具侵占性的物种却利用了这一变化。菹草（Potamogeton crispus）是侵入性最强的水生植物之一，它开始形成大片草岛，河水把成团的草带往下游。一位埃及疟疾专家证实，冈比亚按蚊又利用了菹草，借它把蚊幼虫从一个孳生区运往另一个孳生区。

en: If the gambiae mosquito benefited from the changes in the flow and chemistry of the Nile, its parasite, needing human bodies for reproduction, was also able to take advantage. As a spore-forming parasite, the plasmodium did not set out to kill its human victims, but entered their bodies merely to complete its unusual life cycle. Transferred by the bite of the female mosquito, the young spores take up residence for about a week in the cells of the victim’s liver. Each spore then bursts apart and releases into the bloodstream up to forty thousand offspring, which feed off the blood’s cell hemoglobin and multiply into further offspring, some of which assume separate male and female forms. The explosive reproduction is not intended to kill the victim, but to ensure that with the bite of another mosquito a number of spores are ingested back into the stomach of the insect, where they fertilize and complete the reproductive cycle. However, the malignant form of the parasite brought by the new invader to southern Egypt makes the red blood cells of its victims particularly sticky, clogging the arteries and depriving the body of oxygen. Most victims survive after a severe fever, which ensures that the parasite still has hosts in which to live. But if the brain or another vital organ is deprived of oxygen, the unwilling host can die.
zh: 如果说冈比亚按蚊得益于尼罗河流量及化学性质的变化，那么需要人体来繁殖的寄生虫也得以从中获益。作为一种形成孢子的寄生虫，疟原虫并不是为了杀死人类受害者而来；它进入人体，只是为了完成自己不寻常的生命周期。雌蚊叮咬时把幼小的孢子转移到人体内，它们在受害者的肝细胞中停留约一周。随后，每个孢子裂开，向血流中释放多达四万个后代；这些后代以血细胞中的血红蛋白为食，继续增殖，其中一些分别形成雄性和雌性的形态。这种爆发式繁殖并不是为了杀死受害者，而是要确保另一只蚊子叮咬时，能把一定数量的孢子再次吸入昆虫胃内，使它们在那里受精，完成繁殖周期。然而，新入侵者带到埃及南部的这种恶性寄生虫，会使受害者的红细胞格外黏稠，堵塞动脉，使身体缺氧。多数受害者在经历严重发热后活了下来，这保证了寄生虫仍有可栖居的宿主。但如果脑部或其他重要器官缺氧，这个并非自愿接纳它的宿主就可能死亡。
body.review: 底本以spores泛称疟原虫的不同阶段，并称其堵塞arteries（动脉），这是简化的生物学叙述。CDC的生命周期说明区分子孢子、裂殖子和配子体；雌蚊吸入的是配子体。本文保留原文，而不把这些不同阶段静默改写为同一种规范术语。

en: In Upper Egypt the plasmodium found a population with no immune response to interrupt its infection cycle, for it was a new arrival. It also found a population whose bodies had been transformed by the sugar industry. From the 1920s Egypt’s newly independent government was for the first time able to protect local manufacturing, in particular sugar production, the country’s oldest and largest modern industry. Price protection against the global market in the 1930s and 1940s combined with the irrigation work supported the extension of cultivation. Perennial irrigation and cane cultivation reduced the fertility of the soil and the land available for food production. When the war interrupted the supply of artificial fertilizer, these factors combined to make the people of southern Egypt far more vulnerable to the plasmodium parasite. In contrast to the badly nourished residents of southern Egypt, none of the government officials, medical workers, or eradication teams, nor the wealthy women from Cairo who launched a charity relief operation in the south, lost their lives in the epidemic.
Furthermore, reports from Brazil indicate that sugarcane juice, which those working on sugar plantations consumed on site by breaking and chewing the cane, can worsen the effects of malaria.

Thus on several levels the parasite found that sugar had left the bodies it encountered less able to resist infection. The chemistry of the epidemic operated at the level of the nation and of the cell.
zh: 在上埃及，疟原虫遇到的人群没有能够打断其感染周期的免疫反应，因为它是新来的。它也遇到了一群身体已被制糖业改变的人。从20世纪20年代起，新近独立的埃及政府首次能够保护本国制造业，尤其是制糖业——这个国家历史最久、规模最大的现代工业。20世纪30年代和40年代，对全球市场实行的价格保护与灌溉工程相结合，支持了种植面积的扩张。常年灌溉和甘蔗种植降低了土壤肥力，也缩减了可用于粮食生产的土地。当战争中断人工肥料供应时，这些因素共同使埃及南部居民更容易受到疟原虫侵害。与营养不良的南部居民形成对照的是，政府官员、医务人员、灭蚊队员，以及那些从开罗来到南方开展慈善救济的富裕妇女，无一在疫情中丧生。
此外，巴西的报告表明，甘蔗汁会加重疟疾的影响，而甘蔗种植园的工人会在劳作现场折断甘蔗，咀嚼吸汁。
因此，寄生虫在多个层面发现，糖使它所遇到的身体更难抵抗感染。疫情的化学作用同时发生在国家层面和细胞层面。

en: The fertilizer shortage that contributed to malnutrition also represented the interaction of forces on several levels. After German nitrate supplies were cut off by the war, there was a larger reason why alternative sources of chemical fertilizer could not be found. Natural supplies of ammonium nitrate were available in only one place in the world, the Atacama Desert in Chile, and the U.S. processing companies operating there could supply Egypt with only small amounts. Along with the manufacturers of artificial nitrates, they were using their fertilizer factories for a more urgent purpose. Ammonium nitrate provided the main ingredient for two chemically similar but socially different processes, each concerned with life and death: the fertilizing of crops and the making of high explosives. Europe and America had converted their fertilizer plants to the manufacture of wartime ammunition. The lack of nitrates for Egyptian agriculture, and the consequent food crisis that left much of the population undernourished, was due not only to the loss of a particular source of supplies. The chemical powers of the nitrates contributed to the course of events.
zh: 造成营养不良的肥料短缺，也体现了多层面力量之间的相互作用。德国硝酸盐供应被战争切断后，之所以找不到替代性的化肥来源，还存在一个更大的原因。天然硝酸铵的供应只存在于世界上的一个地方——智利阿塔卡马沙漠，而在那里经营的美国加工公司只能向埃及提供少量产品。它们同人工硝酸盐制造商一样，正把肥料工厂用于一个更迫切的目的。硝酸铵是两种化学上相似、社会上却不同的过程的主要原料；这两种过程都与生死攸关：给作物施肥，以及制造烈性炸药。欧洲和美国已经把肥料厂改为生产战时弹药。埃及农业缺乏硝酸盐，进而发生使大量人口营养不足的粮食危机，并不只是因为失去了某一个特定的供应来源。硝酸盐的化学力量参与塑造了事件的进程。
body.review: 底本此处确写ammonium nitrate（硝酸铵）。USGS《Mineral Resources in Deserts》把阿塔卡马历史上用于肥料与炸药的天然矿物明确列为sodium nitrate（硝酸钠）。此处化学名称疑误，译文保留底本。

en: Finally, war provided the method used to defeat the epidemic, for pyrethrum sprays and Paris green were not enough. After the first winter of the epidemic the government declared the gambiae mosquito eradicated, but in 1943–44 there was a second and much more severe outbreak. Part of the problem was that the eradication campaign, influenced by current public health concerns about the unhealthiness of stagnant water, had concentrated on the large standing pools often found on the edges of villages, whereas this particular mosquito was willing to breed in the smallest ditches and irrigation channels and in the borrow pits left by the construction of railway embankments, which were not associated with disease and were often overlooked.
zh: 最后，战争还提供了战胜疫情的方法，因为除虫菊喷雾和巴黎绿并不足够。疫情经历第一个冬天后，政府宣布冈比亚按蚊已经被根除，但1943—1944年又出现了第二轮、且严重得多的暴发。问题的一部分在于，灭蚊运动受当时公共卫生观念的影响，认为积水有害健康，因而把注意力集中在村庄边缘常见的大型积水池上；但这种特定的蚊子却愿意在极小的沟渠、灌溉水道，以及修筑铁路路堤留下的取土坑中孳生。人们没有把这些地方同疾病联系起来，常常将其忽略。

en: The Egyptian government was able to turn for help to a new form of transnational secular body, the nonprofit corporation. Early in the century, U.S. military expansion in the Caribbean, in particular the building of the Panama Canal, had encouraged extensive efforts to control mosquitoes, which carried both malaria and yellow fever. (Ferdinand de Lesseps, the man who organized the construction of the Suez Canal, had been the first to attempt to dig a canal across the Isthmus of Panama, but in 1889 was forced to abandon the ten-year effort, in part because of deaths from these two diseases.) In 1915, the year after the canal’s completion, the newly established Rockefeller Foundation took over the mosquito campaign from the U.S. army and launched a worldwide program to study and control the two mosquito-borne diseases. Thus the global movements of the mosquito gave shape to a transnational corporate philanthropy.
zh: 埃及政府得以向一种新型跨国世俗组织——非营利法人——求助。世纪初，美国在加勒比地区的军事扩张，尤其是巴拿马运河的修建，推动了大规模灭蚊工作，因为蚊子同时传播疟疾和黄热病。（组织修建苏伊士运河的费迪南·德·雷赛布，也是第一个尝试开凿贯穿巴拿马地峡运河的人；但1889年，他被迫放弃了这项已进行十年的工程，部分原因正是这两种疾病造成的死亡。）1915年，也就是运河建成后的第二年，新成立的洛克菲勒基金会接手美国陆军的灭蚊运动，启动了一项研究和控制这两种蚊媒疾病的全球计划。因此，蚊子的全球移动塑造了一种跨国法人慈善事业。

en: Yellow fever was a more immediate concern than malaria, for it threatened to use the Panama Canal to cross into the Pacific. Rockefeller set up a program in Brazil to eliminate the disease from the coastal areas of South America.

The leader of the campaign, Dr. Fred Soper, developed eradication methods based on modern warfare, in which “brigades” of uniformed men armed with spray guns went on search and destroy missions. Disease was to be defeated not by improved social conditions or medical intervention but by the physical elimination of the enemy species. Detailed maps and index cards recorded the location of houses to be searched, the discovery of each mosquito, and the routes and timing of missions to spray or dump the chemicals. With its focus on yellow fever, the Rockefeller Foundation headquarters in New York was not interested in reports that the gambiae mosquito had reached Brazil. However, Soper saw in the arrival of the new and relatively well contained

an ideal opportunity to demonstrate his technical methods. He organized a campaign in 1938 that eradicated gambiae malaria by the early 1940s. The success made Soper the world’s most influential malaria expert, able to reshape tactics and lay down the new methods of total species eradication, methods that were not seriously challenged for another fifty years.
zh: 相较于疟疾，黄热病是更迫在眉睫的威胁，因为它可能借巴拿马运河进入太平洋。洛克菲勒基金会在巴西设立项目，以消除南美洲沿海地区的黄热病。

运动的负责人弗雷德·索珀医生开发了以现代战争为基础的根除方法：身穿制服、手持喷雾枪的人组成“旅”，执行搜索与歼灭任务。疾病将通过物理消灭敌方物种来战胜，而不是通过改善社会条件或医疗干预。详细的地图和索引卡记录着待搜查房屋的位置、每只蚊子的发现情况，以及喷洒或倾倒化学品的路线与时间。纽约的洛克菲勒基金会总部把注意力放在黄热病上，对冈比亚按蚊已抵达巴西的报告并不感兴趣。不过，索珀认为，这种新来且分布范围相对有限的冈比亚按蚊，为展示他的技术方法提供了理想机会。他于1938年组织了一场运动，到20世纪40年代初根除了冈比亚按蚊传播的疟疾。这次成功使索珀成为世界上最有影响力的疟疾专家，能够重塑战术，并制定彻底根除一个物种的新方法；此后又过了五十年，这些方法才受到严肃挑战。

en: In November 1942, in coordination with the British offensive at al-Alamein, the United States entered the Mediterranean war, landing troops in French North Africa. Disease was again a concern, but in this case it was typhus, which had killed tens of thousands of soldiers in World War I. To develop ways to protect its forces, Washington set up a Typhus Commission with its headquarters in Cairo. Fred Soper of the Rockefeller Foundation was seconded to the commission and sent to Egypt. As in Brazil, his arrival on an unrelated mission coincided with an outbreak of gambiae malaria.

The intersecting networks of U.S. philanthropic and military power had once again brought Soper and the gambiae mosquito together. He drew up a plan for a military-style eradication campaign, but the British authorities, objecting to this introduction of an American influence into Egyptian politics, forced the government to shelve the plan. When the epidemic reemerged in 1943–44, the British began to fear that it threatened the population centers and troop concentrations of the north. They agreed that the Egyptians should appoint “a sort of malaria dictator” to organize a campaign against the disease (the word “dictator” was in vogue in those days).
They were forced to drop their earlier objections and allow the Egyptian government to follow the Brazilian model of eradication, advised by Soper.
The Egyptian teams finally identified and destroyed the last gambiae larvae in February 1945, a few kilometers to the south of ʿAmm Ibrahim’s village near Luxor.
zh: 1942年11月，为配合英军在阿拉曼的攻势，美国投入了地中海战场，在法属北非登陆。疾病再次成为一个关切，但这次是斑疹伤寒——它曾在第一次世界大战中夺走数万名士兵的生命。为了研究保护军队的方法，华盛顿设立了斑疹伤寒委员会，总部设在开罗。洛克菲勒基金会的弗雷德·索珀被借调到该委员会，并被派往埃及。与巴西的情形一样，他为另一项任务而来，却恰逢冈比亚按蚊疟疾暴发。
美国慈善权力与军事权力交织的网络，再一次把索珀与冈比亚按蚊带到了一起。他拟定了一项军事式的灭蚊计划，但英国当局反对美国势力借此进入埃及政治，迫使政府搁置计划。1943—1944年疫情再起时，英国人开始担心，它会威胁北方的人口中心与军队集结地。他们同意埃及方面任命“一种疟疾独裁官”，组织抗疫运动——“独裁官”一词在当时很流行。
他们不得不放弃此前的反对，允许埃及政府在索珀指导下采用巴西的根除模式。
1945年2月，埃及灭蚊队终于在卢克索附近、阿姆·易卜拉欣所在村庄以南几公里处，发现并消灭了最后一批冈比亚按蚊幼虫。

en: The chain of events in Egypt seems to create a triangle, formed by the interconnection of war, disease, and agriculture. War in the Mediterranean diverted attention and resources from an epidemic arriving from the south, brought by mosquitoes that took advantage of wartime traffic. The insect also moved with the aid of the prewar irrigation projects and the ecological transformations those brought about. The irrigation works made water available for industrial crops but left agriculture dependent upon artificial fertilizers. The ammonium nitrate used on the soil was the main ingredient in the manufacture of explosives and was diverted for the needs of war. Deprived of fertilizer the fields produced less food, so the parasite carried by the mosquito found its human hosts malnourished and killed them at the rate of hundreds a day.
zh: 埃及这一连串事件似乎构成了一个三角形，由战争、疾病与农业相互联结而成。地中海的战争把注意力和资源从南方袭来的疫情上移开；蚊子利用战时运输，把疫情带了过来。昆虫的移动还得到战前灌溉工程及其造成的生态转变的帮助。灌溉工程为工业作物提供了用水，却也使农业依赖人工肥料。施入土壤的硝酸铵是制造炸药的主要原料，因而被转用于战争需要。没有肥料，田地生产的粮食减少，于是蚊子携带的寄生虫遇到了营养不良的人类宿主，每天夺走数百人的生命。

en: The chain is in fact more than a triangle. The connections between a war, an epidemic, and a famine depended upon connections between rivers, dams, fertilizers, food webs, and, as we will see, several additional links and interactions. What seems remarkable is the way the properties of these various elements interacted. They were not just separate historical events affecting one another at the social level. The linkages among them were hydraulic, chemical, military, political, etiological, and mechanical. No one writing about Egypt in this period describes this interaction. There are studies of military tactics, irrigation methods, Anglo-Egyptian relations, hydraulic engineering, parasites, the sugar industry, and peasants. But there are no accounts that take seriously how these elements interact. It is as if the elements are somehow incommensurable. They seem to involve very different forces, agents, elements, spatial scales, and temporalities.
They shape one another, yet their heterogeneity offers a resistance to explanation.
zh: 事实上，这条链不止是一个三角形。战争、疫情与饥荒之间的联系，取决于河流、大坝、肥料、食物网之间的联系，以及我们还将看到的若干其他环节和互动。引人注意的是，这些不同要素的性质究竟以怎样的方式相互作用。它们并非只是在社会层面彼此影响的独立历史事件。它们之间的联结涉及水力、化学、军事、政治、病因与机械。没有任何研究这一时期埃及的人描述过这种互动。有关军事战术、灌溉方法、英埃关系、水利工程、寄生虫、制糖业和农民的研究都有，却没有叙述认真对待这些要素如何相互作用。仿佛这些要素在某种意义上不可通约。它们似乎涉及截然不同的力量、行动者、要素、空间尺度和时间性。
它们相互塑造，但其异质性却抵抗着解释。

en: The resistance may have something to do with the mixing of natural and social worlds. Chemical and biological processes are surely of a different order than military and political forces. Each of these processes and forces has its own science, which identifies the agents, time lines, geo-spatial scales, and modes of interaction appropriate to its analysis. This tends to leave each of them isolated in their separate sciences. The isolation may be appropriate for the task of a particular science or technical expertise, but its limitations are striking as soon as one begins to ask about the kinds of interactions I have described. Since those interactions belong, as I suggested, to some of the most profound transformations of the modern era, this presents a problem for social science. Instead of developing the kinds of analysis that might address these interactions, responding to the techno-scientific transformations of the twentieth century, social theory is still largely trapped in the methods and divisions of labor of the nineteenth century.
zh: 这种抵抗或许与自然世界和社会世界的混杂有关。化学与生物过程，无疑同军事和政治力量属于不同层次。每种过程与力量都有自己的科学，确定适用于其分析的行动者、时间线、地理空间尺度和互动方式。这往往使它们各自孤立于所属学科之中。对于某一门科学或某一种技术专长的任务而言，这种隔离也许是合适的；但只要开始追问我所描述的那些互动，其局限便立即凸显。既然这些互动如我所说，属于现代时期一些最深刻的转变，这就给社会科学提出了一个问题。社会理论并未发展出能够处理这些互动、回应20世纪技术科学转变的分析方式，而是在很大程度上仍然受困于19世纪的方法和劳动分工。

en: There are two characteristics of social explanation relevant to this problem. First, social theory typically operates by relating particular cases to a larger pattern or process. Events in a place like Egypt are explained as the local occurrence of something more general, or an exception to what generally occurs, or a particular variation in the general range of possibilities. In some of the social sciences this aim is quite explicit, expressed in rules of method and styles of writing. In others it is implicit but still at work, for example in historical scholarship, in which the narrative may focus on a specific context but draws its structure and relevance from an implied comparison with other, more general cases. Inevitably the generic case in such accounts is the history of Europe or the West, and the particulars of what happened outside Europe are explained as replicas of Europe’s history, or variations from that historical pattern, or alternatives to it.

In studies of Egypt, for example, events like those I have been describing fit into a variety of larger narratives: the story of the nation and its development, the growth of new social classes and other national actors, and the rise of the modern state, often placed in the context of the development of capitalism, the expansion of Europe, or the global history of modernity. The story takes it shape from the way it fits into a sovereign narrative told about every place, the story of rationalization, technological and social progress, the growth and transformation of production, and the universalization of the culture and power of the West. This assumption of a universal armature is the foundation that makes social theory possible. The development of forms of explanation placing particular events into a universal framework coincided, of course, with a quite palpable expansion of Western power, wealth, and technical knowledge. The issue is not whether such expansion occurred, but its relationship to the grounds on which social theory is built. The universal to which social theory aspires is a category founded within and expressed by the particular history of the West.
zh: 社会解释有两个特征与这一问题相关。首先，社会理论通常通过把特定案例与一种更大的模式或过程联系起来而运作。像埃及这样的地方所发生的事件，被解释为某种更普遍现象的地方性发生，或通常情形之外的例外，或一般可能性范围内的一种特殊变体。在某些社会科学中，这一目标十分明确，通过方法规则与写作风格表现出来。在另一些学科中，它虽是隐含的，却仍在发挥作用。例如在历史研究中，叙述可能聚焦于特定情境，但其结构和意义却来自它同其他更一般性案例之间的暗含比较。此类叙述中的一般案例，不可避免地是欧洲或西方的历史；欧洲以外发生的具体事件，则被解释为欧洲历史的复制品、相对于该历史模式的变体，或它的替代形式。

例如在埃及研究中，我一直描述的那些事件，会被纳入各种更宏大的叙事：民族及其发展的故事、新社会阶级与其他民族行动者的成长，以及现代国家的兴起；这些又常被放到资本主义发展、欧洲扩张，或现代性的全球历史之中。故事之所以采取某种形态，是因为它被嵌入一套用于讲述每个地方的支配性叙事——理性化、技术与社会进步、生产的增长与转变，以及西方文化和权力普遍化的故事。对这样一种普遍性骨架的预设，是社会理论得以成立的基础。当然，把特定事件置于普遍框架之中的解释方式的发展，恰好伴随着西方权力、财富与技术知识非常切实的扩张。问题不在于这种扩张是否发生，而在于它同社会理论赖以建立的基础之间是什么关系。社会理论所向往的普遍性，是在西方的特殊历史内部奠基、并由这段历史表达的一个范畴。

en: The second feature of social explanation follows from the first: all the actors are human. The protagonists of the history of the nation, of modernity, of capitalism, are people. Human beings are the agents around whose actions and intentions the story is written. This is necessarily the case, for it is the intentionality or rationality of human agents that gives the explanation its logic and enables particular cases to fit as instances of something general. The general or universal aspect of events that social theory attempts to identify occurs precisely as the spread of this human reason, technical knowledge, or collective consciousness. By contrast, although the river Nile is transnational, and anopheles mosquitoes are quite global, their generality is not the same as that of capitalism, the idea of the nation, or modern science. The Nile is not considered an abstraction, nor is the mosquito experienced as an expression of the universal.
zh: 社会解释的第二个特征由第一个特征而来：所有行动者都是人。民族史、现代性史、资本主义史的主角，都是人。故事围绕人类行动者的行动和意图而书写。这必然如此，因为正是人类行动者的意向性或理性，赋予解释以逻辑，并使特定案例能够作为某种一般现象的实例而纳入其中。社会理论试图辨认的事件之一般性或普遍性，恰恰表现为这种人类理性、技术知识或集体意识的扩散。相比之下，尽管尼罗河是跨国的，按蚊也相当具有全球性，但它们的一般性不同于资本主义、民族观念或现代科学的一般性。尼罗河不被视为一种抽象，蚊子也不被体验为普遍性的表达。

en: The result of these two features of social theory is that in the explanation of events one always knows in advance who the protagonists are. Emile Durkheim once described the resistance that nature offers to understanding compared to the ease with which society is explained. “While the scientist who studies physical nature is very keenly aware of the resistance it offers him, and which he has so much difficulty in overcoming, the sociologist seems to move in a sphere perfectly transparent to his view, so great is the ease with which the most obscure questions are resolved.”

What is this ease, this transparency? It arises in part from having already decided who counts as an agent. It is not that social analysis necessarily ignores disease, agriculture, chemicals, or technology, but that these are externals—nature, tools, obstacles, resources—whose role is essentially passive. Even on the occasions when they are given a more independent force, there is still a fundamental divide between human agency and the nonhuman elements.
zh: 社会理论这两个特征带来的结果是，在解释事件时，人们总是预先知道谁是主角。埃米尔·涂尔干曾经比较过：自然对理解构成阻力，而社会却轻而易举地得到了解释。“研究物质自然的科学家十分敏锐地意识到，自然对他构成了阻力，而克服这种阻力何其困难；社会学家却似乎置身于一个在他眼中完全透明的领域，连最晦暗的问题都能如此轻易地得到解决。”
这种轻易、这种透明，究竟是什么？它部分来自人们早已决定了谁才算是行动者。社会分析未必忽略疾病、农业、化学品或技术，而是把它们当作外在之物——自然、工具、障碍、资源——其作用本质上是被动的。即便偶尔赋予它们较为独立的力量，人类能动性与非人要素之间仍存在一道根本分界。

en: Social science is always founded upon a categorical distinction between the ideality of human intentions and purposes and the object world upon which these work, and which in turn may affect them. There is little room to examine the ways they emerge together in a variety of combinations, or how so-called human agency draws its force by attempting to divert or attach itself to other kinds of energy or logic. No explanation grounded in the universalizing force of human projects and intentions can explore whether the very possibility of the human, of intentionality, of abstraction depends on, at the same time as it overlooks, nonhuman elements. These appear merely physical, secondary, and external.
zh: 社会科学始终建立在一种范畴性区分之上：一边是人类意图与目的的观念性，另一边是这些意图与目的作用于其上、并反过来可能影响它们的对象世界。几乎没有空间去考察，两者如何在多种组合中共同涌现，或所谓的人类能动性如何通过试图转引其他形式的能量或逻辑、或依附于它们而获得力量。任何以人类计划和意图的普遍化力量为基础的解释，都无法探究：人、意向性和抽象之所以可能，是否一面依赖着非人要素，一面又忽视着它们。这些要素显得只是物质性的、次要的和外在的。

en: If the web of events in wartime Egypt offers a certain resistance to explanation, part of the reason may be that it includes a variety of agencies that are not exclusively human: the anopheles mosquito, the falciparum parasite, the chemical properties of ammonium nitrate, the 75mm guns of the Sherman tank, the hydraulic force of the river, and one or two more to be introduced shortly. These do not just interact with the activities of human agents. They make possible a world that somehow seems the outcome of human rationality and programming. They shape a variety of social processes, sometimes according to human plans, but just as often not, or at least not quite. How is it, we need to ask, that forms of rationality, planning, expertise, and profit arise from this effect?
zh: 如果说战时埃及的事件之网对解释构成某种抵抗，部分原因或许在于，它包含了多种并非纯粹属于人的能动作用：按蚊、恶性疟原虫、硝酸铵的化学性质、谢尔曼坦克的75毫米炮、河流的水力，以及稍后还将介绍的一两种力量。它们不只是同人类行动者的活动相互作用。它们使一个世界成为可能，而这个世界不知怎的又显得像是人类理性与规划的产物。它们塑造着各种社会过程，有时遵循人类计划，但同样经常不遵循，或至少不完全遵循。我们需要追问：理性、规划、专门知识与利润的各种形式，究竟是如何从这种效果中产生的？

en: In social theory there is an important exception to the rule that human action is put at the center and the external world is treated as an arena for such action rather than the source of forms of agency and power. It is found in the work of Marx. For Marx, individual capitalists are to be understood not as agents in their own right, but as those who personify the power of capital. The “main-spring” that powers the movement of capitalist history is not human intention but the expansion of value through the exchange of commodities, in particular the exchange of labor power. An individual possessor of money becomes a capitalist, Marx writes, when this expansion of capital through exchange becomes his subjective aim. He then “functions as a capitalist, that is, as capital personified and endowed with consciousness and a will.”

Thus Marx understands capital as something twofold. It arises from the circulation of money, the development of technical processes, and particular patterns of commodity exchange and power relation. Yet these material processes acquire a quasi-human form. Through exchange, the powers of objects take on a consciousness and a will. Most analyses that draw on Marx move quite quickly over this idea. The ability of certain historical actors to personify the force of capital is easily taken for granted. There might be disagreement over which particular actors achieve this role, and how successfully they accomplish it. But what does it mean for capital to become personified? How exactly do nonhuman things or processes form this hybrid with the consciousness of humans? What does it mean to think of capital as something whose power depends on being simultaneously human and nonhuman? Marx, as Derrida says, was “one of the first thinkers of technics,” the first to grapple with the hybrids of man-machine, capital-consciousness, automatism-will.

His writing grasped that human consciousness is an artifactual body, even if in the end he always wanted to ground his critique of consciousness in absolute distinctions between real and abstract, presence and representation, object and value, labor and ideas. These are distinctions whose apparent stability we must explore. How is the ambivalent relation between the nonhuman and the human, or the real and the abstract, constituted? How are the irreducible exchanges or tensions between the two resolved in modern politics into so simple an opposition?
zh: 社会理论通常把人类行动置于中心，并把外部世界当作这种行动的场所，而非能动性与力量之形式的来源；但这一规则有一个重要例外，见于马克思的著作。对马克思而言，个别资本家不应被理解为凭自身而行动的主体，而应被理解为使资本力量人格化的人。驱动资本主义历史运动的“动力”，不是人的意图，而是通过商品交换，尤其是劳动力交换而实现的价值增殖。马克思写道，当这种通过交换实现的资本增殖成为一个货币所有者的主观目的时，他便成了资本家。此时，他“作为资本家起作用，也就是说，作为人格化的、具有意识和意志的资本起作用”。

因此，马克思把资本理解为一种双重之物。它产生于货币流通、技术过程的发展，以及特定的商品交换和权力关系模式。然而，这些物质过程又取得了一种准人的形式。通过交换，对象的力量获得了意识和意志。大多数借鉴马克思的分析，都很快越过了这一观念。某些历史行动者能够使资本力量人格化，这种能力很容易被视为理所当然。人们也许会争论，究竟哪些行动者承担了这一角色，他们完成得有多成功。但资本被人格化，究竟意味着什么？非人的事物或过程，究竟如何同人的意识组成这种混合体？如果资本的力量取决于它同时既是人的又是非人的，那么这样理解资本意味着什么？正如德里达所说，马克思是“最早思考技术的思想家之一”，也是最早着手处理人—机器、资本—意识、自动性—意志这些混合体的人。
他的写作把握到，人类意识是一种人为制成的构成体，尽管最终他总想把对意识的批判建立在一些绝对区分之上：实在与抽象、在场与表象、对象与价值、劳动与观念。我们必须探究这些区分表面上的稳定性。非人与人、或实在与抽象之间这种含混的关系，是如何构成的？在现代政治中，两者之间不可化约的交换或张力，又是如何被化解成如此简单的对立的？

en: To begin this task, we need to find a capitalist, someone who can function in our story as capital personified. Fortunately there is such a capitalist available, and a big one. As it happens he had a large house on the same plantation at Armant mentioned above, where eighty or ninety workers a day were dying of malaria. He was, it will be no surprise to learn, the plantation’s owner. Ahmad ʿAbbud also controlled the processing mill five hundred yards down the river, together with the eighteen other large sugar factories in Egypt that made up the country’s sugar industry, and he was one of the most powerful figures in Egyptian business and politics.

Trained as an engineer at the University of Glasgow, he had worked on irrigation schemes in Ottoman Iraq before World War I and on the railway system in Syria and Palestine during the war. He started business in Egypt in 1924 by obtaining a contract to dredge and maintain the new government-financed irrigation canals, his wealth expanding with the expansion of the public irrigation system.

His construction company worked on increasing the height of the Aswan Dam in 1929–33 and other large state projects. Like a handful of other successful entrepreneurs, he used these lucrative government contracts and concessions to move into other business sectors, including shipping, public transport, real estate, trade, and banking. He joined Egypt’s new class of big landowners by acquiring the six-thousand-acre sugar plantation at Armant, and in 1939 took control of the Egyptian Sugar Company, the country’s oldest and largest industrial venture, which enjoyed a state-protected monopoly over the processing of raw cane and the sale and export of sugar.

By the outbreak of World War II, as his business empire moved its headquarters into Cairo’s first high-rise structure, the eighteen-story Immobilia Building, ʿAbbud controlled one of just two or three family-based entrepreneurial groups competing to monopolize large sectors of the country’s finance, trade, transportation, and industry. Following the war, the international press was to rank him as one of the ten richest men in the world.
zh: 要开始这项工作，我们需要找到一位资本家，一位能在我们的故事中充当人格化资本的人。幸好确有这样一位资本家，而且是位大资本家。巧的是，在前文提到的阿尔曼特种植园——每天有八九十名工人死于疟疾的地方——他就有一座大宅。想必读者不会惊讶，他正是那座种植园的主人。艾哈迈德·阿布德还控制着顺流而下五百码处的加工厂，以及埃及另外十八座大型糖厂；这些工厂共同构成了全国的制糖业。他是埃及商界与政界最有权势的人物之一。
他在格拉斯哥大学接受工程师训练，第一次世界大战前曾在奥斯曼帝国治下的伊拉克从事灌溉工程，战争期间则在叙利亚与巴勒斯坦的铁路系统工作。1924年，他获得了一份疏浚和维护政府出资新建灌溉渠的合同，由此在埃及开始经商；随着公共灌溉系统的扩展，他的财富也不断增长。
他的建筑公司参与了1929—1933年阿斯旺大坝的加高工程，以及其他大型国家项目。同其他少数成功企业家一样，他借助这些利润丰厚的政府合同与特许权，进入航运、公共交通、房地产、贸易和银行等其他商业领域。他购入阿尔曼特那座六千费丹的甘蔗种植园，加入埃及新兴的大地主阶层；1939年，他又控制了埃及糖业公司。这是全国历史最久、规模最大的工业企业，在国家保护下垄断着甘蔗原料加工以及糖的销售和出口。
到第二次世界大战爆发时，他的商业帝国将总部搬入开罗第一座高层建筑——十八层的伊莫比利亚大楼。此时，阿布德控制着全国仅有的两三个家族企业集团之一，它们正争相垄断本国金融、贸易、运输和工业中的大片领域。战后，国际报刊会将他列为世界十大富豪之一。
body.review: 本章的acre按作者原注67专指Egyptian acre，即feddan。译文统一作‘费丹（埃及亩）’，不换算为英制英亩。

en: The growth of ʿAbbud’s empire depended upon his making and remaking circuits of political and social power. In February 1942 the British forced the appointment of an Egyptian government led by the Wafd party, which had earlier negotiated the country’s partial independence from Britain and seemed its most reliable wartime ally. Through a business association with the Wakil family, cotton merchants and landowners whose daughter Zaynab was married to the Wafdist prime minister, ʿAbbud reestablished earlier ties with the Wafd, began to finance its activities, and helped put his allies and business associates in control. Three months after the party took power, ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Wakil, a brother of ʿAbbud’s business partner, was made minister of health, just as the ministry received the first news of the arrival of gambiae malaria.

At the same time ʿAbbud secured the dismissal of the Wafd’s new minister of finance, who had tried to introduce sugar rationing (and to prosecute the Wakils for the wartime smuggling of cotton textiles).

The minister’s removal gave ʿAbbud’s sugar monopoly a free hand to negotiate a lucrative deal with the British. As the negotiations neared completion in February 1943, the British ambassador spent six weeks visiting ʿAbbud and his Scottish-born wife Jemima at their spacious red-tiled villa on the sugar estate (a long anticipated trip that became a “nightmare” after the ambassador suffered a dangerous fever and ʿAbbud was twice almost killed, first in a plane crash and then in a driving accident when his horse bolted and threw him against a brick wall).

Following the stay ʿAbbud concluded his “thief’s bargain,” as the disgruntled British called it in private, agreeing to sell the British military authorities his company’s “surplus” stock of sugar (at a moment of famine on the sugar estates) for a considerable profit. The deal also gave ʿAbbud scarce supplies of fertilizer, officially earmarked for other crops, to use on the sugar plantations.
zh: 阿布德帝国的成长，依赖于他不断建立并重组政治与社会权力的回路。1942年2月，英国强迫埃及任命了一个由华夫脱党领导的政府；该党早先通过谈判争取到了埃及对英国的部分独立，看起来也是英国最可靠的战时盟友。阿布德通过与瓦基勒家族的商业往来，重新建立了早年同华夫脱党的关系，开始资助其活动，并帮助自己的盟友与商业伙伴掌握权力。瓦基勒家族既经营棉花贸易，又拥有土地；其女儿宰娜卜嫁给了华夫脱党籍首相。该党执政三个月后，阿布德商业伙伴的兄弟阿卜杜勒·瓦希德·瓦基勒被任命为卫生部长，恰逢该部收到冈比亚按蚊疟疾抵达埃及的第一批消息。
与此同时，阿布德促成了华夫脱党新任财政部长的免职；后者曾试图实行食糖配给，并起诉瓦基勒家族在战时走私棉纺织品。
部长被免职，使阿布德的糖业垄断企业能够放手同英国谈判一笔厚利交易。1943年2月，谈判接近完成时，英国大使到阿布德和他出生于苏格兰的妻子杰迈玛家中访问，在糖业庄园那座宽敞的红瓦别墅住了六个星期。这是一次期待已久的旅行，却变成了“噩梦”：大使患上危险的发热病，阿布德也两度险些丧命，先是遭遇飞机失事，随后又在驾车时因马匹惊奔，被甩撞到砖墙上。
大使离开后，阿布德达成了那笔令不满的英国人在私下称作“强盗买卖”的交易，同意以可观的利润，把公司“剩余”的糖库存卖给英国军事当局——而此时糖业庄园正发生饥荒。交易还使阿布德获得了稀缺肥料，用于甘蔗种植园，尽管这些肥料官方原本指定供其他作物使用。

en: Over the following months, as the malaria epidemic took hold again, ʿAbbud embarked on an audacious scheme to use his profits from the sugar deal and the expansion of cane cultivation to make himself into what a British official, invoking once again the nomenclature of the day, called “a kind of commercial dictator.”

ʿAbbud maneuvered to take over the bank and the affiliated enterprises of the country’s other major business conglomerate, the Misr group, which had a dominant position in textile manufacture, the cotton trade, air transport, cinema, insurance, and other fields.

At the same time he revived a plan from the 1930s for Egypt’s largest industrial scheme, to install hydroelectric turbines in the dam at Aswan that had recently been made higher. He proposed to use the electricity to manufacture and supply the country’s entire demand for fertilizer.
zh: 此后的几个月，疟疾疫情再度蔓延，阿布德则展开了一项大胆计划，要利用食糖交易和扩大甘蔗种植所得的利润，把自己变成一位英国官员再次借用当时流行用语所说的“一种商业独裁者”。
阿布德运作着要接管埃及另一个主要企业集团——米斯尔集团——的银行和附属企业。该集团在纺织制造、棉花贸易、航空运输、电影、保险及其他领域占据支配地位。
与此同时，他重启了20世纪30年代的一项计划：在新近加高的阿斯旺大坝安装水力涡轮机，建设埃及最大的工业工程。他提议利用所发的电制造肥料，满足全国的全部需求。

en: The interwar years had seen a growing struggle among the rival business groups for the dominant position in what Robert Vitalis calls the “rent circuits” of Egyptian politics, meaning the profits to be made from privileged control of the economic resources circulating through the country. Controlling the circulation of rents, however, was dependent upon the control of resources that had other, interconnected forms of circulation. These included the complex networks of family power and colonial affiliation whose significance I have already suggested. But at the center of these struggles from the 1920s to the 1950s was an effort to command, or at least turn to profit, one particular kind of circuit, the flow of the waters of the Nile.

The Aswan Dam offered the opportunity to reorganize and concentrate into fewer hands a series of further circulations—hydraulic, electrical, political, chemical, and agricultural. ʿAbbud and his rivals competed for the lucrative rights to build a hydroelectric power station at Aswan and convert the force of the river’s flow into the power to drive industry, which in turn would fuel agriculture. Large quantities of electric power would be used to convert nitrogen into artificial fertilizer. Just as alluvial silt had once been carried and deposited by the floodwaters of the Nile, synthetic chemicals would in future be transported in sacks from the nitrate plant at Aswan and deposited across the country’s fields to restore a little of the lost fertility of the soil. The complex flows of the Nile flood, channeled into storage basins, held for several weeks to allow silt and nutrients to settle, and released again into the river, were to be reorganized and transformed into the narrower flows of waters through turbine wheels, high voltages along transmission cables, electrical energy into nitrates, fertilizer sacks across the countryside, and ammonia from the soil into the proteins of cane and cotton plants. The political struggle to control rent circuits was a battle to build and control these interconnected circuits. And it was through these same circuits—dams, irrigation, sugar cultivation—that the mosquito had entered Egypt.
zh: 两次世界大战之间，竞争中的企业集团为争夺埃及政治中罗伯特·维塔利斯所谓“租金回路”的支配地位，展开了日益激烈的斗争。所谓租金回路，指的是凭借对流经这个国家的经济资源享有特权控制而获取的利润。然而，控制租金的流转，又依赖于控制那些具有其他相互关联的流转形式的资源。这包括复杂的家族权力与殖民关系网络，其重要性我已经有所提示。但从20世纪20年代到50年代，这些斗争的中心，是试图支配、或至少从中获利的一种特定回路——尼罗河水的流动。

阿斯旺大坝提供了机会，使一系列其他流转——水力、电力、政治、化学和农业的流转——能够重新组织，并集中到更少的人手中。阿布德与其对手争夺在阿斯旺兴建水电站的高利润权利，要把河流的水力转化为驱动工业的动力，再由工业供给农业。大量电力将被用于把氮转化为人工肥料。正如冲积淤泥曾由尼罗河洪水携带并沉积下来一样，未来，合成化学品将装袋从阿斯旺的硝酸盐工厂运出，撒向全国田野，恢复土壤已经丧失的一小部分肥力。尼罗河洪水的复杂流动——被引入蓄水盆地、留存数周以让淤泥和养分沉降、再被排回河道——将被重新组织和转化为更狭窄的流动：水穿过涡轮，电力以高电压沿输电线传送，电能转入硝酸盐，肥料袋运往乡间，氨从土壤转入甘蔗和棉株的蛋白质。控制租金回路的政治斗争，就是一场建立并控制这些相互联结的回路的斗争。而蚊子也正是经由同样这些回路——大坝、灌溉、甘蔗种植——进入埃及的。

en: Should we explain ʿAbbud’s power and wealth in terms of his ability to “personify” capital and become the conscious representative of its power to reproduce and expand? This seems preferable to the alternative of saying that ʿAbbud’s success resulted simply from his skill as a calculating agent who was able to out-calculate his rivals and make an ever larger profit. The latter explanation attributes all the success to ʿAbbud himself. It does not even ask what arrangements (of law, property, political economy, engineering, irrigation, and much more) made such calculation possible, or what agencies kept those arrangements in place. The former at least gives some credit to another power, the circulating force of capital. Capital can circulate and, by combining with further forces, go through metamorphoses into other forms—from money into property and labor, property and labor into sugarcane, sugarcane into processed sugar or al-cohol, and back again into money—using resources and arrangements that do not come from ʿAbbud alone.

Clearly, however, the movements and metamorphoses of capital were not the only circulations at work in ʿAbbud’s success. His struggle to divert rent circuits to his own advantage was at the same time an effort to develop and direct a whole series of interconnected circuits: water, electricity, nitrates, military requisitions, cane, processed sugar, cotton, and several others.
zh: 我们是否应该这样解释阿布德的权势和财富：他能够使资本“人格化”，并成为资本自我再生产和扩张力量的自觉代表？相比另一种解释——阿布德的成功仅仅源于他善于算计，能够比对手算得更精，并获取越来越大的利润——这种说法似乎更好。后一种解释把成功全归于阿布德本人。它甚至没有追问：究竟是哪些安排——法律、财产、政治经济、工程、灌溉，以及更多安排——使这种计算成为可能？又有哪些能动作用维持着这些安排？前一种解释至少承认了另一种力量，即资本流通的力量。资本能够流通，并通过与其他力量结合而蜕变为其他形式：从货币变为财产和劳动，从财产和劳动变为甘蔗，从甘蔗变为加工后的糖或酒精，再重新变回货币；它所利用的资源和安排，并非仅由阿布德提供。
然而，显然，在阿布德的成功中发挥作用的流转，不只有资本的运动与形态变化。他试图把租金回路转为己用的斗争，同时也是发展并引导一整套相互联结回路的努力：水、电、硝酸盐、军方征购、甘蔗、加工糖、棉花，以及其他若干回路。

en: Clearly, too, the idea that these circulations and forces are “personified,” or represented by the actions of particular individuals, is too simple. Individuals may at times secure control of certain elements, and they may even claim to represent those elements in the social world. But no individual masters them, or submits the world to their intentions. More often there occurs a series of claims, affinities, and interactions, all of which exceed the grasp or intention of the human agents involved. Human agency and intention are partial and incomplete products of these interactions. This incompleteness, as we will see, means that no single line divides the human from the nonhuman, or intentions and plans from the object-world to which they refer.
zh: 同样明显的是，认为这些流转与力量被“人格化”，或由特定个人的行动加以代表，这个想法过于简单。个人有时也许能够控制某些要素，甚至声称在社会世界中代表着这些要素。但没有哪个人能够完全驾驭它们，或让世界服从自己的意图。更多时候出现的是一系列诉求、亲和关系与互动，它们全部超出了相关人类行动者的把握或意图。人类能动性与意图，是这些互动的局部而不完整的产物。我们将会看到，这种不完整性意味着：不存在一条单一界线，可以把人与非人分开，或把意图和计划同它们所指向的对象世界分开。

en: But why insist on all these additional agencies, circulations, and forces? Surely the task of social science, like all science, is to simplify, to identify a limited number of more decisive agents. Why not accept a simpler but more powerful story, one that can depict the big picture and even identify certain patterns or predictions? There is an old answer to this question: that if the world is a complicated and indeterminate place, with many agencies and forces at work, then an accurate picture of that world will be a complex and indeterminate one.

But the answer I want to propose here has to do with the role of expertise and reason, explanation and simplification, in the politics of the twentieth century. Politics itself was working to simplify the world, attempting to gain for itself the powers of expertise by resolving it into simple forces and oppositions.
zh: 但为什么要坚持纳入所有这些额外的能动作用、流转与力量？社会科学的任务，难道不应像一切科学一样，是进行简化，辨认数量有限、更加具有决定性的行动者吗？为什么不接受一种较为简单却更有解释力的叙事，一种能够描绘全局、甚至辨认出某些模式或作出预测的叙事？对此有一个老答案：如果世界本就是复杂且未定的，存在许多发挥作用的行动者与力量，那么对它的准确描绘也必然是复杂且未定的。
但我在这里想提出的答案，涉及专门知识与理性、解释与简化在20世纪政治中的作用。政治本身就在努力简化世界，试图通过把世界归结为简单的力量与对立，为自己取得专门知识的权力。

en: This is not, therefore, a question of introducing a natural or hydraulic determinism to replace the determinism of modern technological innovation or capitalist expansion. If social and economic networks were connected with the changing ecology of one of the world’s longest rivers, this does not mean attributing social outcomes to changes in nature. Long before the Aswan Dam, before all the irrigation work of the nineteenth century, the river was already as much a technical and social phenomenon as a natural one. Its waters were channeled, stored, raised, distributed, and drained by the interaction of mechanical, human, animal, and hydraulic power. William Willcocks, the director of reservoirs for the Egyptian government, whose studies of Nile hydraulics were used to determine the engineering of the Aswan Dam, considered the old system of channeling floodwaters in sequence into hundreds of interconnected field basins, holding them for a certain period, and releasing them in sequence again into the river a more complex irrigation mechanism than the enormous but singular barrage and reservoir that replaced it.
The old methods had manufactured a geography that was no more natural than it was human, and no less. Rather, it was always both.
zh: 因此，这并不是要引入自然决定论或水力决定论，来替代现代技术创新或资本主义扩张的决定论。如果社会和经济网络同世界最长河流之一不断变化的生态相联结，这并不意味着要把社会结果归因于自然变化。早在阿斯旺大坝之前，早在19世纪所有那些灌溉工程之前，这条河就既是技术与社会现象，也是自然现象。其河水由机械、人、动物与水力的相互作用加以引导、储存、提升、分配和排放。埃及政府水库主管威廉·威尔科克斯对尼罗河水力的研究，被用于确定阿斯旺大坝的工程设计。他认为，旧有灌溉系统把洪水依次引入数百个相互连通的田间盆地，留存一定时间，再依次排回河道；这样的灌溉机制，比取而代之的庞大却单一的拦河坝与水库更为复杂。
旧方法制造出一种地理，它的自然性并不比人造性更多，也并不更少。毋宁说，它始终兼具两者。

en: Nature was not the cause of the changes taking place. It was the outcome. The very scale of the technical and engineering works of the twentieth century produced a new experience of the river Nile as exclusively a force of nature. A visit to the Aswan Dam inspired a European writer to publish the first popular account of the river, which he called a “biography” of its life. “When, at the end of 1924, I first saw the Great Dam at Aswân,” wrote Emil Ludwig, “its symbolic significance burst upon me with such force that I seemed to comprehend the River Nile forwards and backwards from this crucial point in its course. A mighty element had been tamed by human ingenuity so that the desert should bring forth fruit, an achievement which the centenarian Faust had attempted as the highest attainable to man in the service of his fellow-men.”

The reference to Faust is quite appropriate. Goethe’s great novel of the colonizing transformation of nature was inspired by conversations with Saint-Simonians, secular priests of engineering who had traveled to Egypt in the nineteenth century and initiated the irrigation projects completed, and transformed, with the Aswan Dam. The new scale of twentieth-century engineering, of which the Aswan Dam was among the first and most dramatic examples anywhere in the world, turned the bizarre religion of the Saint-Simonians into an everyday belief: that “human ingenuity” could now dominate the “mighty elements” of nature. In manufacturing the dam, the engineers also manufactured nature.
zh: 自然不是正在发生的变化的原因，而是其结果。正是20世纪技术与工程建设的规模，产生了一种把尼罗河纯然体验为自然力量的新方式。一位欧洲作家在参观阿斯旺大坝后受到启发，出版了第一部通俗的尼罗河叙述，并称之为这条河生命的“传记”。埃米尔·路德维希写道：“1924年底，当我第一次看到阿斯旺大坝时，它的象征意义如此强烈地扑面而来，我仿佛能从河道上这个关键点，向前向后理解整条尼罗河。一股强大的自然力量已被人类的才智驯服，使沙漠能够结出果实；百岁的浮士德也曾尝试这项成就，视之为人服务于同胞所能达到的最高境界。”
这里提到浮士德十分贴切。歌德这部关于以殖民方式改造自然的伟大小说，受到他与圣西门主义者谈话的启发。这些人是工程的世俗祭司，他们在19世纪前往埃及，开创了后来随着阿斯旺大坝而完成并转变的灌溉工程。20世纪工程的新规模——阿斯旺大坝是全世界最早也最引人注目的例子之一——把圣西门主义者那种奇异的宗教变成了日常信念：“人类才智”如今能够支配自然的“强大力量”。工程师在制造大坝的同时，也制造了自然。
body.review: 底本将《浮士德》称作novel（小说），这里照译。魏玛古典基金会作品目录将其列为Drama（戏剧），并称为悲剧。

en: Several features of the new construction helped produce the effect of a world divided into human expertise on one side and nature on the other. First, there was the concentration of the river control mechanisms at one site. The old irrigation mechanisms were distributed along the length of the valley, formed out of hundreds of canals, drains, dikes, basins, sluices, pumps, and water wheels, as well as the channel of the river itself, and drew upon steam, animal, hydraulic, and human power. It would have been difficult in describing these arrangements to say where natural forces ended and technology began, or to draw a line between ingenuity and nature. In contrast, the dam at Aswan gathered all the engineering into one location, providing an observation point where writers like Ludwig could stand and suddenly “comprehend” the river as a force of nature tamed by man. Second, the concentration of engineering required a parallel concentration of capital. Building the original dam cost £2,440,000 sterling, and a further £280,000 was spent to strengthen the base immediately after the reservoir was filled.

To organize, and later justify, this expenditure required a series of proposals, plans, financial statements, political memoranda, annual reports, and newspaper accounts, all of which in different ways described, enumerated, calculated, and argued about the building of the dam. The arguments and calculations accompanying the old hydraulic system had been distributed over a much wider territory. Thus a significant reorganization and concentration of accounting, calculation, description, and knowledge accompanied the concentration of hydraulic power in the dam. These and other reorganizations were the kinds of processes through which the world came to be simplified into what seemed nature on one side, and human calculation and expertise on the other.
zh: 这项新建设的若干特征，帮助产生了一种效果：世界被分成两边，一边是人类的专门知识，另一边是自然。首先，河流控制机制集中到了一个地点。旧有的灌溉机制分布在整个河谷，由数百条渠道、排水沟、堤坝、盆地、闸门、水泵和水车，以及河流自身的河道构成，并利用蒸汽、动物、水力与人力。在描述这些安排时，很难说自然力量在哪里结束、技术在哪里开始，也很难在才智与自然之间画出界线。相比之下，阿斯旺大坝把全部工程集中到一个地点，提供了一个观察位置；路德维希这样的作家可以站在那里，突然“理解”这条河是一种被人驯服的自然力量。其次，工程的集中要求资本相应集中。最初的大坝造价为244万英镑，而水库蓄水后，为加固坝基立即又花了28万英镑。
要组织这笔支出，并在后来为其辩护，就需要一系列建议书、计划、财务报表、政治备忘录、年度报告与报刊报道；所有这些都以不同方式描述、列举、计算和争论大坝的建设。围绕旧有水利系统的论证与计算，则分布在广阔得多的地域。因此，随着水力集中于大坝，核算、计算、描述和知识也发生了重大的重组与集中。正是通过这些及其他重组过程，世界逐渐被简化为：一边仿佛是自然，另一边则是人类计算与专门知识。

en: Life was now to be increasingly resolved into this binary arrangement, rendering up a simple, dualistic world of nature versus science, material reality versus human ingenuity, stonework versus blueprints, objects versus ideas. This dualism, however, as the Aswan example indicates, was an artifact of particular projects and politics. Like all dualisms, and all artifacts, it was neither original nor completely stable. The artifactual is the effect of a process.

If one turns back from the effect created by the engineering at Aswan, from the force of the “symbolic” that Ludwig was able to experience when standing before the completed dam, to recover the process itself, then the distinction between nature and science, between masonry and symbol, between the river to be tamed and the expertise that later claimed to have tamed it, one can locate any number of episodes, elements, and forces that disrupt the effect created by the final artifact. Engineering the dam was a messy, uncertain, conflict-ridden, and haphazard project. Public finances were controlled by an International Debt Commission, which forced changes in the alignment of the dam. The original plan had allowed “more play and choice of alignment” to take advantage of the soundest rock for the foundations. Instead, the granite under the foundation was rotten, causing delays to the construction and uncertainty about its future stability. The delays forced the contractors to abandon plans to build the masonry work using mortar manufactured from local lime and to import ready-made, faster-drying Portland cement instead. The cement mortar was less flexible and watertight than lime, leading to problems with leakage through the structure. The water spilling through the dam’s sluices began to erode its base. The engineers had neglected to consider thermal stresses. The dam cost twice the original budget.

Subsequent problems of silt accumulation, seepage, and evaporation from the reservoir were so great that instead of increasing the water available, the mean annual discharge of water below the dam was almost one-fourth less in the fifty years following the dam’s construction than in the thirty years before it was built.

None of these problems was foreseen by the experts at work on the dam. So complex were the forms of calculation required by dam construction, it later gave rise to the new field called cost-benefit analysis. But as hundreds and eventually thousands of large dams were built around the world in the course of the century, the accuracy of calculation cannot be said to have improved.
zh: 生活如今越来越被归入这种二元安排，呈现出一个简单的二元世界：自然对科学，物质现实对人类才智，砌石工程对蓝图，对象对观念。然而，阿斯旺的例子表明，这种二元论是特定工程与政治的人造产物。同一切二元论和一切人造物一样，它既非原初存在，也不完全稳定。人造性是一个过程的效果。

如果从阿斯旺工程所创造的效果——从路德维希站在已建成的大坝面前所体验到的“象征”力量——回过头去，重新找回过程本身，那么，在自然与科学、砌体与象征、待被驯服的河流与事后声称已驯服它的专门知识这些区分之中，就能发现许多事件、要素和力量，扰乱着最终人造物所产生的效果。大坝工程是一项混乱、不确定、冲突重重且充满偶然性的事业。公共财政受国际债务委员会控制，该委员会迫使工程改变坝线。原方案允许“在坝线选择上有更大的余地”，以便利用最坚固的岩石作地基。实际采用的坝基花岗岩却已风化腐坏，导致施工延误，也使大坝未来的稳定性变得不确定。延误迫使承包商放弃使用当地石灰制成砂浆进行砌筑的计划，转而进口干燥更快的成品波特兰水泥。水泥砂浆不及石灰柔韧、防水，造成坝体渗漏。流经泄水闸的水开始侵蚀坝基。工程师还忽略了热应力。大坝造价达到最初预算的两倍。
此后，淤泥堆积、水库渗漏与蒸发的问题如此严重，以至于水量非但没有增加，建坝后五十年中坝下年均径流量，反而比建坝前三十年减少了将近四分之一。
参与大坝建设的专家没有预见到这些问题中的任何一个。筑坝所需的计算形式极其复杂，后来甚至催生了一个叫作成本—收益分析的新领域。但在这个世纪里，随着世界各地兴建了数百座、最终数千座大坝，不能说计算的准确性有所提高。

en: Still, it might be argued, science one by one solved the problems it encountered. Many of them were overcome, it is true, but then one would have to acknowledge that science did not direct the engineer’s work as a preformed intelligence. The projects themselves formed the science.

Solutions were worked out on the ground. Engineering was an expertise given shape in these and similar undertakings. The British engineers returned to London after each season of construction in Aswan to present papers at meetings of the Institution of Civil Engineers. These were published in the
of the institution, or in professional journals such as
